scenes.name: Naked funk: la era Reagan
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: La era del naked funk abarca las cimas de Prince, Michael Jackson y los dos mandatos de Reagan: recortes, desindustrialización, millones de sin techo, la «guerra contra las drogas» en lugar de contra la pobreza y, desde 1982, el crack. La música negra se volvió narcisista y escapista, del «yo primero»; las bandas, demasiado caras para la ciudad. La industria ofrecía estereotipos (banda pop, crooner, banda funk guarra, según Jon Pareles), MTV no ponía vídeos negros hasta Thriller y Jackson y Prince marcaron las cuotas del crossover. En 1975 trece números 1 R&B eran funk; en 1985 diecisiete de veinte eran baladas. Warner echó a Clinton y CBS sepultó «Pumpin’ It Up»; murieron o se convirtieron Hathaway, Joe Tex, Marvin Gaye, Al Green, Larry Graham. Las máquinas sustituyeron vientos, órgano (el Yamaha DX7), batería y bajo: solo sobrevivió la guitarra rítmica sobre el bajo sintetizado y la palmada electrónica. La insinuación dejó paso al sexo explícito sin cerebro («Do Me Baby», «Beep a Freak»), y llegaron el bass de Miami (2 Live Crew), Egyptian Lover, el New Jack Swing de Teddy Riley y la farsa de Milli Vanilli. Los funkers de verdad abandonaron la radio: el underground (hip hop, go-go) llevó el funk adelante.

podcast.title: Grammys Scandal and Pop's Credibility (1990)
podcast.body: The Milli Vanilli Grammys scandal contributed to pop music proving itself to be a "hollow sham," further driving its decline by 1990. "pop had proven itself to be a hollow sham thanks to the Millie Vanille Grammys scandal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Pop Dominance in Early 1990s
podcast.body: Milli Vanilli contributed to the pop music sound that ruled at the very beginning of the 1990s, before a series of events and the rise of Generation X ushered in the era of grunge and alternative music. "At the very beginning of the decade, pop music ruled Michael Jackson, Janet Jackson, Maddon, Millie Vanilley, and new kids on the block."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 1: Rock Struggles Again

podcast.title: Scandal over Lip Syncing
podcast.body: Milli Vanilli were infamously "hounded out of the music business" following revelations that they were lip-syncing in live performances and were not the actual vocalists on their records. This incident became a cautionary tale in the music industry, highlighting the severe repercussions for perceived dishonesty in performance authenticity. "Millie Vanillie were hounded out of the music business for doing this."

xref.title: Death in German Hotel (April 3, 1995)
xref.body: Rob Pilatus, one half of the pop duo Milli Vanilli, was found dead in a German hotel room on April 3, 1995, due to an overdose of prescription drugs and alcohol. "Rob Pilatus, one half of the disgraced Pap Duo Millie Vanillee, was found dead in a German hotel room on April 3, 1995, an OD of prescription drugs and alcohol."
